ai_technology: DDRTree in Monocle 2; modified k-nearest-neighbor projection; MissForest

evidence.ai_role: DDRTree learned a branching representation of age/sex-adjusted clinical measures and continuous profile scores; modified nearest-neighbor projection transferred the learned framework to the SSC cohort for comparison with clinical and genetic features.
evidence.tested: Retrospective discovery in 6,355 SPARK participants and projection into 2,717 SSC participants, with clinical/service/medication associations and common- and rare-genetic-variant analyses. DDRTree parameters were refined against clinical observations; external projection used imputed/harmonized measures.
evidence.unknown: The proposed profiles are not validated diagnostic categories, treatment-selection rules or causal genetic explanations. Genetic analyses were preliminary and some findings did not reproduce in SSC; cohort size, imputation and phenotype harmonization limit inference.

organization: University of Southern California; Simons Foundation

source_review.scope: Primary 29-page v1 PDF relevant clinical/genetic Results, DDRTree/projection Methods and limitations; primary Research Square embedded version metadata and Crossref posting metadata. Supplements were not independently audited.

summary: A November 23, 2026 preprint used DDRTree to learn three clinical profiles and continuous scores from 14 measures in 6,355 autistic children in SPARK, then projected the framework into 2,717 children in the Simons Simplex Collection. The authors report preserved clinical and medication-use patterns and preliminary differences in common- and rare-variant associations. These are retrospective, researcher-tuned dimensions, not established diagnostic categories or causal genetic mechanisms; some genetic results differed between cohorts and require larger-sample validation.
title: Learned autism profiles show different clinical and genetic associations
